approved: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill 2015

The bill enhances the Veterans' Vocational Rehabilitation Scheme, streamlines the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act appeal process, and amends the Defence Act to allow repatriation of eight service dependants from Terendak Military Cemetery in Malaysia, with the government investing over $12 billion in veterans' services.

The bill expands the Veterans' Vocational Rehabilitation Scheme to allow intermediate rate disability pensioners to work up to 20 hours a week without pension reduction and to set a higher minimum pension for special rate participants, creates a single review pathway for original determinations under the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act, and authorises the repatriation of the remains of eight service dependants buried at Terendak Military Cemetery in Malaysia.

The speaker supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill 2015, which enhances vocational rehabilitation and streamlines appeals, and announced the repatriation of 25 Vietnam War servicemen and eight service dependants from Terendak and Kranji cemeteries at government expense, criticising the member for Solomon and noting personal involvement in recovering Private David Fisher's remains.

The bill enhances the Veterans' Vocational Rehabilitation Scheme with $700,000, creates a single appeal path under the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act, and expands war graves regulation to include service dependents at Terendak Military Cemetery. The government also announced $10 million for additional case coordinators and over $12 billion in Veterans' Affairs services, including $6.5 billion for pensions and $5.5 billion for healthcare.

The speaker supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill 2015, which expands vocational rehabilitation services, streamlines the appeals process, and allows repatriation of the remains of service dependents. The bill also supports the government's offer to repatriate the 25 Australian soldiers and eight dependents still buried in Malaysia and Singapore from the Vietnam War.

The member for Solomon supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill 2015, citing its three components that simplify military rehabilitation and compensation processes, and thanked Senator Ronaldson for repatriating fallen soldiers, including Reg Hillier, whose body will be returned to the Adelaide River War Cemetery. The member also expressed disappointment that the previous minister for veterans' affairs did not act on this issue.

The Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill expands the Veterans Vocational And Rehabilitation Scheme to include medical, management and psychosocial services, allows special and intermediate rate disability pension recipients to retain more pension, and streamlines MRCA appeals to a single path via the Veterans' Review Board. It also amends the Defence Act to enable repatriation of eight service dependants buried in Terendak Military Cemetery if families request it.

Labor supported schedules 1 and 3 of the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (2015 Budget Measures) Bill 2015, which enhance the Veterans' Vocational Rehabilitation Scheme and expand war graves powers to repatriate remains from Terendak Military Cemetery, while agreeing to defer schedule 2—streamlining veterans' appeals—for further negotiations in 2016.

Schedule 2 of the bill, proposing a single appeal pathway for veterans, was removed for further negotiations, while schedule 3 authorises the exhumation of dependants' remains from Terendak Military Cemetery, with families deciding on repatriation.
